title: Ask dev: a reader-visible register of unverified, unsupported and disputed statements (the editor's request of 29 October 2026)
note: From breaking@php.newsroom, at the editor's word in its session on 29 October 2026 ('these kinds of issues we should capture on a sort of unsupported or unverified statements'). Why: the Dream Research report (breaking-0005) is a single-source account of 25 compromised servers; the newsroom carries it as 'reported, not independently confirmed', but nothing lists such statements in one place, so a reader or a lane cannot see what we are carrying without proof, why, or what would settle it. What exists: data files/vault-claims.json already carries a status on every claim (29 October: reported 463+, confirmed 48, unverified 42+, disputed 39, contradicted 1) and files/claim-review.json carries the journalist's verdicts, including 'held back'. Proposal (dev decides the shape and where it lives): a derived file, for example files/unverified-statements.json, built from those two files (no hand-kept copy), one row per statement: claim id, the statement in one line, who made it, status (unverified, unsupported, disputed), why it is not confirmed (single source, evidence withheld, a relay of another outlet, a contradiction), what would confirm or end it, first seen, last reviewed, and when and how it closed (confirmed, withdrawn, contradicted). Then a page for it (the editor: unsupported or unverified statements) and a line on the state of affairs. First entries: the Dream Research claims cur29 to cur31, cur34, cur37, cur40 to cur42 and the CyPro conflict cur57/cur58, listed with reasons in the debrief article of 29 October (the correspondent's lane, written at the editor's request). A new data file needs tools/catalogue.json (dev) and a schema; the press would build the page. Nothing is written for this by the desk.
